title: Make sense of English tenses
intro: Choose a card for uses, structures and examples. Explore one group at a time, connecting meaning with form.
verbGuidePreview: Choose the right verb before choosing its form · Side-by-side examples
verbGuideIntro: Start with what you want to say, then choose the verb form. “Other main verbs” can be regular or irregular. Be itself can also function as a main verb.
mainBeText: Use be to link a subject to a noun (identity), an adjective (description/state) or a place. An additional action verb is unnecessary.
mainBeExamples: I am tired. · She is a doctor. · They are at home.
otherVerbText: Use the verb that expresses your meaning: work, eat and play for activities; know, like and own for states. Do not automatically add am/is/are before a base verb.
otherVerbExamples: I work here. · I know the answer.
comparisonBeExamples: I am ready. · I am not ready. · Are you ready?
comparisonOtherExamples: I work here. · I do not work here. · Do you work here?
comparisonNote: With be, add not or put be before the subject; do not use do/does. With other main verbs in the present simple, use do/does for negatives and Yes/No questions. In the past simple, be becomes was/were; other verbs use did + V for negatives/questions.
auxiliaryBeText: Be + V-ing forms the continuous; be + V3 can form the passive. Be and another verb can therefore appear together when the structure requires it.
auxiliaryBeExamples: She is studying. · The room is cleaned every morning.
verbGuideMistakes: Incorrect: I am work here. → Correct: I work here. Incorrect: Does she is tired? → Correct: Is she tired? For an action in progress, use I am working.
verbGuideNuance: An adjective does not always require be: I feel tired is also correct (feel is a linking verb). Be also changes with the form: I was tired; I have been busy; I will be ready.
irregularPreview: Look up V1–V2–V3 and meanings · Search in English or Vietnamese
irregularIntro: V2 is used in affirmative past simple clauses. V3 follows have/has/had in perfect forms and be in passive constructions. After did/did not use V1: Did you go?, not Did you went?.
irregularVariants: A selection of common verbs, not an exhaustive list. A slash separates accepted forms; some verbs allow both -ed and irregular forms. Read the notes for meaning and British/American differences.

markersNote: These expressions are clues, not rules. Choose the form from context and meaning, not a keyword alone.
passiveNote: Passives normally require a verb with an object: make the object the subject, put be in the appropriate form, then add V3. By + agent is optional when unnecessary. Be + adjective/noun is not automatically passive.
legend: S: subject · V: base verb without “to” · V2: past form · V3: past participle (-ed or irregular) · V-ing: -ing form · O: object · C: complement (adjective, noun, place phrase…)
questionNote: For information questions, usually put What/Where/When/Why/How before the Yes/No pattern. When Who/What is the subject, do not use that inversion: Who works here?
overviewNote: 12 familiar teaching forms, organised by time and aspect. Future forms here use will; be going to and other ways to express future time also exist.
